To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

jet-broadening cross section factorizes into a hard part and a soft part in a way that is free of collinear anomalies and that the hard part is known to NNLL accuracy and beyond, and the soft part is known to LL accuracy and beyond.
the jet broadening is factorized at the level of distributions and that this factorization is free of the large perturbative corrections in the two-jettiness region.

the factorization theorem for the cross section for the event shape variable jet-broadening is free of large logarithms in the small jet-broadening limit, and that it is given by a sum of a perturbative part and an event-shape dependent non-perturbative part, which is given in terms of a non-perturbatively defined jet-broadening distribution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the resummation of logarithms in the perturbative QCD cross section for the event-shape variable jet broadening.
the factorization and resummation of perturbative corrections to jet-broadening cross sections.
the factorization and resummation of perturbative QCD logarithms for event shape variables in e + e → hadrons.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the factorization formula for jet broadening is valid at next-to-leading order in α s, but it is only valid at leading logarithmic accuracy beyond next-to-leading order.
the factorization formula (1) is correct and that the factorization theorem (2) is correct in the sense that the anomalous logarithms are absent.
we have found a factorized formula for the jet broadening cross section, which is free from large perturbative collinear logarithms in the limit of small jet broadening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have derived an all-order factorized formula for jet-broadened distributions, which is valid for all values of the broadened angle, and which reproduces known results for the two-jet region at next-to-next-to-leading order.
we provide the first all-order resummation of jet-broadening cross sections in QCD.
we have found a way to resum all logarithmically enhanced contributions to jet-broadening observables.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the collinear anomaly of jet broadening is related to the collinear anomaly that appears in resummed jet cross sections.
the collinear anomaly can be understood as a resummation of a class of logarithms in the jet-broadening distribution that can be resummed to all orders in perturbation theory.

jet-broadening is not infrared safe at small jet broadening and that the collinear anomaly can be traced back to a nontrivial interplay between the infrared behavior of jet-broadening and the jet mass.
